quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Quarterly Sales] Regional sales rose by 5 percent in the quarter. Sales in the north, however, fell for the second quarter in a row, and the report adds that the northern manager "has been reassigned."
quests.question: Which statement is best supported by the report?
options: Growth elsewhere is hiding a continuing decline in the north.
Sales fell in the north because other regions took its customers.
Sales in the north are likely to recover under the new manager.
The regional rise is caused by strong sales in the north.
quests.correctAnswer: Growth elsewhere is hiding a continuing decline in the north.
quests.hint: Separate the region's overall figure from the figure for the north.
quests.explanation: An overall rise combined with two falls in the north means the other areas must have grown more. The report does not say why the manager moved.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Has Shipped] The supplier's email says the parts "have shipped." The tracking link shows that a label was created on Monday, but no carrier has scanned the parcel.
quests.question: What might "shipped" mean here?
options: The parcel has left the supplier's warehouse and is lost in transit.
The supplier has sent the parcel to the wrong address.
The carrier scanned the parcel on Monday but failed to update the link.
"Shipped" may mean only that a label has been printed.
quests.correctAnswer: "Shipped" may mean only that a label has been printed.
quests.hint: What does the tracking page confirm, and what does it not?
quests.explanation: A label exists, but no carrier has scanned it. The supplier's word may mean something less than the customer expects.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [One Year at a Time] In the staff briefing, the manager said, "Nobody's job is at risk this year." Asked about next year, she smiled and said, "Let's take one year at a time."
quests.question: What can employees conclude about job security?
options: She is not promising job security beyond this year.
She is promising that nobody's job is at risk next year.
She is hinting that some jobs will be lost this year.
She is refusing to answer questions about this year.
quests.correctAnswer: She is not promising job security beyond this year.
quests.hint: Compare her answer about this year with her answer about next year.
quests.explanation: The first answer is definite, while the second avoids the question. That suggests she cannot or will not promise anything further.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Quick Sync] The invitation reads "Quick sync (30 min)." The attached agenda has nine items and a note: "Please read the 22-page document beforehand."
quests.question: What should attendees expect?
options: The meeting is likely to run longer than thirty minutes and requires preparation.
The meeting will be quick because the document is only a summary.
The meeting will focus on one item from the nine on the agenda.
The meeting is optional for anyone who has read the document.
quests.correctAnswer: The meeting is likely to run longer than thirty minutes and requires preparation.
quests.hint: Compare the title with the agenda and the note.
quests.explanation: Nine items and a document to read do not fit a "quick" half hour. The description understates the commitment.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Two Lines] Ines's handover note has two lines: "Everything is in the shared folder. Ask Marco if anything is unclear." Marco left the company in March.
quests.question: What is the problem with the handover note?
options: The handover is unnecessary, since Ines is still at the company.
The handover is inadequate, since the named contact is no longer available.
The handover is incomplete, since the shared folder is not organised.
The handover is thorough, since everything is in the shared folder.
quests.correctAnswer: The handover is inadequate, since the named contact is no longer available.
quests.hint: Who does the note tell the reader to ask, and where is that person now?
quests.explanation: The note relies on a person who has left. The reader has no one to ask.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Everyone Who Worked] The director's email thanked "everyone who worked tirelessly on the launch." It then listed the names of five senior managers.
quests.question: How might junior staff feel?
options: Senior managers did most of the work on the launch.
Junior staff who worked on the launch may feel overlooked.
The launch was disappointing, so only managers are thanked.
The director does not appreciate the launch.
quests.correctAnswer: Junior staff who worked on the launch may feel overlooked.
quests.hint: Compare the group that is thanked with the people who are named.
quests.explanation: The email thanks "everyone" but names only the managers, so the wider team is not personally recognised.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Logged] Thank you for contacting us. We take all complaints seriously. Your complaint has been logged (reference 55821), and you should hear from us within 28 days.
quests.question: How does the company respond to the complaint?
options: It promises a solution within 28 days.
It refuses the complaint because the reference number is missing.
It transfers the complaint to another company.
It acknowledges the complaint but does not commit to resolving it.
quests.correctAnswer: It acknowledges the complaint but does not commit to resolving it.
quests.hint: What does the message promise, and what does it not promise?
quests.explanation: It promises a reference number and a reply within 28 days. It does not promise a solution.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Lower Price] Prices displayed include tax. Prices at the register may vary if a shelf label is out of date. We will always charge the lower price if the customer points it out.
quests.question: Who might end up paying more?
options: Customers who do not notice a difference may pay more.
Customers must show a receipt to receive the lower price.
Customers who notice a difference will pay the higher price.
Customers pay less at the register than the labels show.
quests.correctAnswer: Customers who do not notice a difference may pay more.
quests.hint: When will the lower price be charged?
quests.explanation: The lower price depends on the customer pointing it out. Those who do not check may pay the higher one.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Nine or Ten] The card asks: "How likely are you to recommend us?" with a scale from 0 to 10. Below the scale, in small print: "Only scores of 9 or 10 are recorded as positive."
quests.question: What happens to a score of 7 or 8?
options: Only a score of 10 would be counted as positive.
Scores below 5 would be ignored in the results.
A score of 8 would be counted as positive, but a 7 would not.
A score of 7 or 8 would not be counted as positive.
quests.correctAnswer: A score of 7 or 8 would not be counted as positive.
quests.hint: Which scores does the small print name?
quests.explanation: The small print counts only 9 and 10 as positive, so a 7 or 8 is not counted in the positive total.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Printed Books] Early printed books were expensive, so they were mostly bought by institutions. Ordinary readers relied on texts read aloud by others. As printing costs fell, private ownership grew and reading increasingly became a silent activity.
quests.question: What links cheaper printing to reading habits?
options: Ordinary readers preferred hearing texts read aloud.
Silent reading spread because books became shorter.
Institutions stopped buying books when printing became cheaper.
Cheaper printing changed how people read.
quests.correctAnswer: Cheaper printing changed how people read.
quests.hint: Follow the changes in cost, ownership, and reading style.
quests.explanation: The passage links falling costs to more private ownership and then silent reading. The order suggests one led to the other.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Re-Reading] In a trial, students who were tested on material after reading it remembered more a week later than students who simply re-read it. However, the students preferred re-reading and rated it as more effective.
quests.question: What do the results say about how effective methods feel?
options: What feels effective is not always what works best.
Students who preferred re-reading learned the material better.
Testing is probably more enjoyable than re-reading.
Students remember more when they read the material twice.
quests.correctAnswer: What feels effective is not always what works best.
quests.hint: Compare the results with the students' opinions.
quests.explanation: Testing produced better memory, yet the students believed re-reading worked better. Feeling and result diverge.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Word Limit] Answer three questions. Question 1 is compulsory. Marks will be awarded for evidence and reasoning, not for length. Essays over 800 words will not receive additional credit.
quests.question: What does the word limit imply for longer essays?
options: Essays under 800 words will lose marks.
Essays with more evidence receive extra credit above 800 words.
Writing more than 800 words will not raise a mark.
Question 1 will be marked more strictly than the others.
quests.correctAnswer: Writing more than 800 words will not raise a mark.
quests.hint: What does the final sentence say about extra words?
quests.explanation: Credit comes from evidence and reasoning, and words above 800 add nothing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Moon's Face] The moon always shows the same face to Earth because it takes as long to rotate once as it takes to orbit Earth once. The far side is not permanently dark; it receives as much sunlight as the near side.
quests.question: Why is "dark side" not an accurate name?
options: "Dark side" is a misleading name for the far side.
The far side is hidden because the moon does not rotate.
The far side is dark because it cannot be seen from Earth.
The moon's near side receives less sunlight than the far side.
quests.correctAnswer: "Dark side" is a misleading name for the far side.
quests.hint: What does the passage say about sunlight on the far side?
quests.explanation: The far side receives as much sunlight as the near side, so "dark" does not describe it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Three Signals] Scientists monitor a volcano's gas emissions, its small earthquakes, and swelling of the ground. A sudden rise in all three, they say, is "more informative than any one alone."
quests.question: Why do scientists look at three signals together?
options: Scientists can predict eruptions once all three signs rise.
Small earthquakes are probably more useful than swelling.
Volcanoes show gas emissions before any other sign.
A single warning sign can be unreliable.
quests.correctAnswer: A single warning sign can be unreliable.
quests.hint: Why does the passage stress "all three"?
quests.explanation: Combining signals is described as better, which implies that any one signal might mislead.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Reusable Bags] A study found that a supermarket's plastic bags could be reused about ten times before breaking. It also found that most customers reused them fewer than three times.
quests.question: What determines the bags' environmental benefit?
options: The bags are stronger than most customers realise.
The environmental benefit depends on how customers behave.
The bags are designed to be used only three times.
The supermarket should make the bags more expensive.
quests.correctAnswer: The environmental benefit depends on how customers behave.
quests.hint: Compare what the bags can do with what customers do.
quests.explanation: Their potential of about ten uses is unused, so the benefit depends on habit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Since the Update] The app has 4.7 stars from 90,000 ratings. Filtered by "most recent," the last 200 reviews average 2.1 stars, and many mention "since the update."
quests.question: Why do the two ratings differ so much?
options: The overall rating is inaccurate because it counts old ratings twice.
The update fixed problems, and satisfaction is rising.
The update lowered satisfaction, and the overall rating hides this.
Recent reviewers are more critical than earlier ones about all apps.
quests.correctAnswer: The update lowered satisfaction, and the overall rating hides this.
quests.hint: Compare the overall average with the recent one.
quests.explanation: A large number of older ratings holds the average up, while recent reviewers blame the update.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Almost Full] Free accounts include 5 GB. After the change, photos taken on the phone are backed up automatically. Several users have received warnings that their storage is "almost full" within weeks.
quests.question: What do the storage warnings suggest?
options: Automatic backup fills the free space quickly and may push users toward paid plans.
Users take too many photos, and the free account is too small for anyone.
Automatic backup deletes older photos to save space.
The warnings are a mistake, because photos do not use much space.
quests.correctAnswer: Automatic backup fills the free space quickly and may push users toward paid plans.
quests.hint: What now happens automatically, and what did users receive?
quests.explanation: Photos are copied without action from the user, and warnings appear soon after. This suggests the service benefits from users needing more space.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Smart Meters] The energy company says, "Smart meters will help you save money." The leaflet includes a chart showing how much energy each appliance uses. It does not say whether the meters cost anything.
quests.question: What does the leaflet not address?
options: The leaflet shows that meters are free.
The leaflet warns that meters use more energy than appliances.
The leaflet compares the meter's price with other companies'.
The leaflet stresses benefits and leaves out the question of cost.
quests.correctAnswer: The leaflet stresses benefits and leaves out the question of cost.
quests.hint: What does the leaflet include, and what does it omit?
quests.explanation: The leaflet has benefits and information, but no cost is mentioned. We cannot assume it is free.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Rent Increase] Your rent will rise by 4 percent from 1 July, in line with inflation. Advertisements in the area show similar flats being offered at 2 percent above your current rent.
quests.question: How will the new rent compare with similar flats?
options: After the rise, the rent will be slightly above the local asking prices.
After the rise, the rent will be slightly below the local asking prices.
After the rise, the rent will be much higher than the local asking prices.
After the rise, the rent will match the local asking prices.
quests.correctAnswer: After the rise, the rent will be slightly above the local asking prices.
quests.hint: Compare 4 percent with 2 percent.
quests.explanation: The new rent is 4 percent above the current one, and similar flats are 2 percent above it. So the new rent exceeds them by about 2 percent.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Real Terms] "Your pension pot has grown by 3 percent this year," the letter says. Inflation over the same period was 5 percent.
quests.question: What does the pension's growth mean in real terms?
options: The pot has grown in value because it rose by 3 percent.
The pot has kept pace with the cost of living.
In real terms, the pot has lost value.
The pot has lost 5 percent of its value.
quests.correctAnswer: In real terms, the pot has lost value.
quests.hint: Compare the growth with the rise in prices.
quests.explanation: Growth of 3 percent buys less when prices rise 5 percent, so the purchasing power has fallen.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Wear and Tear] Cover for accidental damage is included. Damage caused by "wear and tear or gradual deterioration" is excluded. To claim, you must report the incident within 48 hours.
quests.question: How would a claim for gradual damage be treated?
options: A claim for damage caused by wear would be paid in part.
A claim for accidental damage would be refused as well.
A claim for slowly developing damage would probably be refused.
A claim reported after 48 hours would still be accepted.
quests.correctAnswer: A claim for slowly developing damage would probably be refused.
quests.hint: Which types of damage are covered, and which are excluded?
quests.explanation: Accidents are covered, but gradual damage is excluded. A slow, developing fault would fall in the excluded category.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Three Hours] Passengers are advised to arrive three hours before international departures. Security queues have averaged fifty minutes this month. Check-in closes sixty minutes before departure.
quests.question: Why is such an early arrival advised?
options: It reflects the time needed to reach the terminal from the car park.
It reflects long queues at security.
It reflects the airport's wish to sell more goods in its shops.
It reflects a rule set by the government for all flights.
quests.correctAnswer: It reflects long queues at security.
quests.hint: Which figure in the passage would explain a long recommended time?
quests.explanation: The advice to arrive early appears with the fifty-minute average queue, which suggests that the queue is a main reason.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Last Entry] Open daily 10 to 5. Last entry at 4:15. The Egyptian gallery closes at 4:30 for cleaning.
quests.question: What will a visitor arriving at 4:15 experience?
options: They will have to leave the museum at 4:30.
They can enter the Egyptian gallery after it has been cleaned.
They will have very little time in the Egyptian gallery.
They will not be allowed into the museum.
quests.correctAnswer: They will have very little time in the Egyptian gallery.
quests.hint: Compare the closing time of the gallery with the last entry.
quests.explanation: A visitor entering at 4:15 has fifteen minutes before the gallery closes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Optional Castle] The tour price includes transport, a guide, and lunch. Entry to the castle, at $14, is "optional." The guide calls the castle "the highlight of the day."
quests.question: What will most visitors probably do about the castle?
options: The castle will be included if visitors ask before the tour.
Most visitors will probably pay the extra $14.
Most visitors will avoid the castle because of the price.
The guide will pay the entry for those who ask.
quests.correctAnswer: Most visitors will probably pay the extra $14.
quests.hint: What do the words "optional" and "highlight" say about each other?
quests.explanation: An "optional" extra described as the highlight is one most people will not want to miss, so the real cost is higher.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Recycling Point] Post on the residents' app: "Whoever keeps leaving bags at the recycling point on Sundays, we can see you." Replies: "?", "Not me!", and "Maybe we should all just check the collection schedule."
quests.question: How do the replies respond to the accusation?
options: The neighbours agree that someone is leaving bags on Sundays.
The neighbours think the recycling point is too small.
Not everyone agrees with the accusation, and one person suggests a different explanation.
The neighbours have found the person who left the bags.
quests.correctAnswer: Not everyone agrees with the accusation, and one person suggests a different explanation.
quests.hint: Read the three replies and compare their attitudes.
quests.explanation: The replies show puzzlement, denial, and a suggestion that the problem could be the schedule, not a person.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [School Closure Statement] The board announced that closing the school had been "considered and rejected." The next paragraph said that "all options remain under review."
quests.question: What do the two statements together mean for the school?
options: The school will close after the review.
Closure has not been ruled out for good.
The board has decided to keep the school open next year.
The board has probably not yet considered closing the school.
quests.correctAnswer: Closure has not been ruled out for good.
quests.hint: What does the second paragraph do to the first?
quests.explanation: "All options remain under review" softens the earlier rejection, since closure is included in "all options."

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Fridays] The youth club is open on Tuesdays and Fridays. Attendance on Fridays is three times that on Tuesdays. The funding application asks for "extended Friday hours."
quests.question: Why is the club asking for extended Friday hours?
options: The club has to close on Tuesdays if it opens longer on Fridays.
The club believes Fridays are popular enough to justify more time.
The club wants funding for a new building for Friday sessions.
The club wants to reduce Tuesday sessions to save money.
quests.correctAnswer: The club believes Fridays are popular enough to justify more time.
quests.hint: What does the attendance figure suggest about the request?
quests.explanation: High Friday attendance supports the request for more Friday hours.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Tram Line] It is easy to praise the new tram line for reducing car journeys. It is harder to acknowledge that the bus routes cut to pay for it have left two villages with no evening service.
quests.question: What is the writer's attitude?
options: In favour of the tram line despite the loss of some buses.
Opposed to trams because they are expensive to build.
Critical of the tram line's supporters for overlooking a cost.
Neutral about the tram line and the bus routes.
quests.correctAnswer: Critical of the tram line's supporters for overlooking a cost.
quests.hint: What does "harder to acknowledge" imply about the tram line's supporters?
quests.explanation: The writer grants the benefit but stresses what people prefer to ignore. That reveals a critical stance.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Handover Help] Dear Ms. Lund, I am writing to resign with effect from 30 June. I am grateful for the opportunities I have had here. I have accepted a role elsewhere and will be happy to help with the handover.
quests.question: What does his letter suggest about how he leaves?
options: He is leaving reluctantly and hopes to be asked to stay.
He is leaving because he was unhappy with his work.
He is leaving for a role with the same company.
He is leaving on good terms.
quests.correctAnswer: He is leaving on good terms.
quests.hint: What tone do the middle sentences set?
quests.explanation: Gratitude and willingness to help suggest a cooperative, friendly departure.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Delay Compensation] The airline apologises "for any inconvenience." It then notes that compensation is payable only if a delay was within the airline's control, and that "weather" is not.
quests.question: What is the airline signalling about compensation?
options: The airline is offering compensation to all passengers.
The airline is apologising because the delay was in its control.
The airline is signalling that it will not pay compensation for a weather delay.
The airline is admitting that the weather was not the reason.
quests.correctAnswer: The airline is signalling that it will not pay compensation for a weather delay.
quests.hint: Which statement follows the apology?
quests.explanation: After the apology the airline states a rule and says weather is outside its control. This is a way of declining compensation.
